_doc: tests/reformulation_ordinary_corpus.json - escalation-trigger-rate corpus.
Built to answer a question Stage 6 (VALIDATION.md §6) explicitly could NOT
answer: how often does reformulate.py's T5 restructuring-escalation path
actually trigger, and how often does it succeed, on ORDINARY text — as
opposed to Stage 6's corpus, which was deliberately built failure-mode-
dense (REFORMULATION_RESEARCH.md §17) and is not representative of
typical usage.
Texts: all 36 sentences from tests/eval_corpus.txt (already-committed,
ordinary, non-adversarial — used unmodified, not reworded to hit any
profile), plus 6 ordinary multi-sentence paragraphs written for this
corpus on everyday topics (weather, work, cooking, a museum visit, a
hobby) with no attempt to cluster any particular sound or word.
Profiles: five profiles representative of what a real speaker might
plausibly declare over time — a light single-sound profile, a moderate
two-sound profile, a consonant-cluster profile (clinically documented as
harder than singleton consonants), a words-only profile, and a mixed
profile modeled on the shape of the actual users/default.json seen in
this repo (a small number of sounds + words + one phrase). None of the
42 texts were chosen or altered to make any profile hit harder or
softer than it naturally would.
Every text x profile combination is run once through reformulate.py
only (not the three-way legacy comparison — this question is specific
to the escalation path, which only reformulate.py has).

profiles.name: light_single_sound
profiles.rationale: A single common sibilant onset — the lightest plausible declared profile, e.g. a speaker who mainly blocks on /s/.

profiles.name: moderate_two_plosive
profiles.rationale: Two plosive onsets — plosives are a commonly cited stutter-prone class in the disfluency literature (RESEARCH.md §1.2).

profiles.name: consonant_clusters
profiles.rationale: Three consonant-cluster onsets, clinically documented as harder than singleton consonants — a plausible profile for a speaker whose difficulty is specifically blend-related.

profiles.name: words_only
profiles.rationale: No sounds at all — five ordinary, plausible workplace/everyday words a speaker might specifically flag, independent of any shared onset.

profiles.name: typical_mixed
profiles.rationale: Modeled on the shape of this repo's own users/default.json (one sound, a handful of words, one phrase) — the closest thing to 'what a real populated profile looks like after a few weeks of use'.
